Sun 08 Nov 2026 12:00PM Aldridge Studio Tickets Sun 08 Nov 2026 3:00PM Aldridge Studio Tickets There is only one word used in our show - it’s ‘Hay!’ Like the stuffing in Geenie’s scarecrow, ‘Hay!’ like the sound she makes when he comes to life and ‘Hay!’ when he sees all the wonders of the natural world for the first time. Only one word but so many meanings in a show about growing up in the heart of the countryside and discovering that you don’t have to stay stuck in the mud – you can live your dreams, spread your wings and fly like the birds. A highly accessible show filled with music, clowning, song and dance. In this beautiful story Farmer Geenie guides scarecrow step by step as he finds his feet, then his hands, his voice, his legs and his love of song and dance in a story about the fun of growing up where everyday there’s something new to make you say ‘Hay!’ Our two very talented physical theatre performers are expert clowns and so our show doesn’t use any words – everything is told in a fantastically clear way through sound, dance, music and our incredibly inventive props which playfully represent the essential elements of nature that this show celebrates. We’ve got charming puppets – the birds of course and also the butterflies and bees - and some very wonderful eggs each with their own particular surprises. All of this means that our show is highly accessible and perfect for a younger age-group who will be giggling all the way through this gentle introduction to what theatre can be - sweet, funny, inclusive and uplifting. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Spooky Space at The Science and Industry Museum - Manchester’s Finest Spooky Space at The Science and Industry Museum Sat 24th Oct, 2026 - Sun 1st Nov, 2026 - Science and Industry Museum Spooky Space at The Science and Industry Museum Science and Industry Museum, Liverpool Rd, Manchester M3 4JP Sat 24th Oct, 2026 - Sun 1st Nov, 2026 More info Directions events Go to Manchester's Finest Facebook page Go to Manchester's Finest X profile From Saturday 24 October to Sunday 1 November, The Science and Industry Museum is hosting a programme of scary science activities for Halloween including sci-fi film viewings and big screen gaming. Inspired by the screen, visitors can then create their own extra-terrestrial characters and discover how scientists hunt for signs of life in the cosmos. They’re even hosting a series of animation workshops if you want to bring your creature to life. Adults aren’t left out either as they open the museum up after hours for an evening of drag performances, gaming and spooky-themed food and drink. Check their website for details, as some events require booking in advance. Interested in more events? evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester Metropolitan University has been allocated £16 million from the Greater Manchester Good Growth Fund to establish FUSE-M, a groundbreaking innovation facility bringing together immersive technologies, AI and advanced manufacturing to help businesses develop, test and co The allocation forms a key part of the latest round of investment from the Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA), which has earmarked funding for a range of projects through the innovation strand of its Good Growth Fund FUSE-M (Future User-centred Simulation, Enterprise and Manufacturing) will be a 1,600 sq m business-facing innovation facility located in Hulme, where organisations can explore, test and adopt emerging technologies The project brings together manufacturing expertise from Manchester Met’s award winning advanced additive manufacturing facility PrintCity, and Centre for Digital Modelling and Analysis for Cultural Heritage (D-MACH) facility, alongside creative and digital expertise from the Uni The new facility will be a specialist innovation space providing companies with access to advanced simulation, digital modelling, immersive technologies, digital twins, prototyping and manufacturing capabilities The facility has already attracted support from major industry partners including Siemens, HP, Matsuura, TEKEVER and The Vita Group and will work alongside key regional innovation assets including Atom Valley, Manchester Science Park and the Henry Royce Institute

evidence_packet.evidence_text: This year marks 100 years since Wythenshawe Hall was donated to Manchester Corporation At the time, the city was in urgent need of more housing In 1920 an urban planner called Patrick Abercrombie identified Wythenshawe as the only undeveloped land suitable for building a housing estate close to Manchester To turn his proposal into a reality, Ernest and Shena Simon bought Wythenshawe Hall from Robert Henry Grenville Tatton in 1926, which they donated to the city's corporation (now known as the council) The idea was that people could be rehoused away from industrial Manchester into what became known as the "Garden City" To celebrate 100 years, BBC North West Tonight has spoken to 100 people from the area about what Wythenshawe means to them

What the 27-year-old said next proved a turning point in the investigation into the death of popular head teacher Michael Mullins, who had been struck by a car the previous day and dragged under its wheels for more than a mile Debotte told the astonished Goddard she not only knew who was responsible for hitting the 56-year-old as he cycled home from work, but she witnessed what happened from the passenger seat That night, having initially been treated as a suspect, she sat in the interview suite at Stretford Police Station and named her cousin, 35-year-old former mechanic Simon Richardson, as the driver Thanks in part to the evidence provided by Debotte, Richardson was found guilty of murder after a two-week trial at Manchester's Minshull Street Crown Court

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Work has begun to restore lock gates across Greater Manchester's historical canal network A team has started fitting new handmade gates at Lock 80 on the Rochdale Canal, a waterway opened in 1804 as the first of three trans-Pennine canals, running between Manchester and Sowerby Bridge, West Yorkshire The new gates, at the lock to the east of the city centre in Manchester, were handcrafted from oak in Yorkshire, before being craned into place Each leaf of the upstream gate weighs one-and-a-half tonnes (1,500 kg), and the downstream leaves weigh two-and-a-half tonnes (2,500 kg). evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester FinTech Crediflow AI secures £1.5m Posted on November 4, 2026 by staff Manchester FinTech Crediflow AI secures £1.5m Startup which came through PXN’s PraeSeed programme last year aims to cut manual work behind commercial lending through automation Share: Listen to article FinTech Investment A FinTech company serving banks and specialist lenders has secured £1.5 million in funding. Manchester-based Crediflow AI automates the manual work that goes into preparing and assessing business loans, which limits how many deals lenders can take on and makes smaller loans to SMEs expensive to underwrite. The company has developed a platform that pulls together the information credit teams currently gather and process by hand, such as financial statements, bank transactions and borrower documents, and turns it into structured credit analysis. In practice, the platform extracts and standardises figures from a borrower’s accounts – a process the industry calls financial spreading – analyses cash flow and drafts the memo a lender’s credit committee uses to approve a loan, in each customer’s preferred format. The platform is already used by hundreds of credit professionals across the UK, Europe and the US, supporting lenders of all sizes, from specialist lenders such as AddWorking Capital to global captive finance such as Iveco Capital. Crediflow was founded by CEO Drey Kenfack, who has more than a decade of experience in commercial lending and private credit, including senior credit roles at Ford Credit Bank, DF Capital Bank and Advance Global Capital. The round was led by NPIF II – PXN Equity Finance, which is managed by PXN Ventures as part of the Northern Powerhouse Investment Fund II (NPIF II), with investment also coming from Haatch and angel investors. Moving from Alderley Edge, Clio’s new 5,134 sq. ft office is a turnkey space designed for high-growth businesses, with 50 fixed workstations, dedicated pods and booths for focused work, board and meeting rooms, a kitchen complete with a dining area, and flexible touchdown spaces built to support collaboration. Already home to law firm TLT, accountancy and business advisory firm BDO, and the PE-backed professional services group Leonard Curtis, Eden offers move-in-ready office space designed to make taking on a new workspace simpler and more straightforward. Delivered by ECF, our partnership with Homes England’s National Housing Bank, L&G and Muse , the turnkey model streamlined Clio’s move into its new space, reducing the time and complexity typically associated with a traditional office fit-out. Moving into a city centre location brings Clio closer to its growing UK customer base following its recent acquisition of Manchester-based ShareDo, now Clio Operate , the legal work management platform for large firms and enterprise legal teams. Eden’s central location and modern amenities also support Clio’s continued growth by strengthening its ability to attract and retain talent. Credit: UK Parliament A Labour MP has revealed that she is a victim of domestic abuse - Speaking in the Commons on October 13, Kirith Entwistle, who represents Bolton North East, described her experience of the current court system as "triggering", adding that she had to watch her abuser "stare at her" during a recent video hearing Ms Entwistle told her fellow MPs that she believes special measures - where victims are given protection or assistance in court - should be the standard in cases involving domestic abuse Examples of these measures could include screens, the ability to give evidence through a live link, or witnesses being able to be accompanied when giving evidence Measures to protect victims are included in the Courts and Tribunals Bill, which is currently going through Parliament Speaking during a debate on the bill, Ms Entwistle said: "It doesn’t matter how many times somebody tells me that they understand what I’m going through, or they acknowledge what I’ve been through, they really don’t unless they have lived it themselves or know somebody who has."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan aims to create 200,000 entry-level jobs over the next decade, recognising the barriers facing employers and the importance of regional organisations in connecting people with opportunities. The government has published its D The plan acknowledges that the challenge is not simply a shortage of people with digital skills. Entry-level recruitment has become more difficult, with employers increasingly favouring experienced candidates and many graduates and other new entrants struggling to secure their fi Manchester Digital contributed to the development of the plan through its involvement in the government's Digital Skills Council, drawing on its work with employers and education providers across Greater Manchester Around 800,000 digital and technology roles are projected to need filling over the next decade. The plan sets out an ambition to create 200,000 entry-level jobs, including apprenticeships, during that period The plan also addresses how AI is changing workforce requirements and the importance of ensuring people entering the industry have both technical knowledge and practical workplace skills Manchester Digital's 2026 Sector Insights Report highlighted a reduction of around 20% in early-career opportunities, despite continued demand for experienced technology professionals

He told the MEN his 12-day stay cost £1,634 when he booked it online. But after just one evening, he claims to have woke up with bug bites all over his body The property is understood to have offered the individual a refund since the incident. They labelled them a ‘backwards step’ for and an ‘unwelcome curtailing’ of democra Under the new rules planning applications would be split into two tiers – Schedule 1 applications and Schedule 2 applications, designated by planning officers. Schedule 1 includes smaller and more technical applications that would only be dealt with by planning officers Schedule 2 covers larger applications, which may be brought before the planning committee, if agreed by the planning committee chair and the council’s chief planning officer. The move also removes elected members’ right to ‘call in’ a planning application for scrutiny and debate The new rules came into force at the end of October, with Bury council now having approved the change in its constitution needed to meet the new legal requirements. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bury It has been a police station, a courthouse and a school, now it could be new homes 100 years of history has taken place in these buildings Add to preferred sources Comments News Hannah Richardson 14:36, 26 Oct 2026 View 2 Images The former Bury G Buildings which once formed part of Bury Grammar School could now get a new lease of life Plans have been submitted to Bury council to convert part of the old school estate into new homes. The three buildings, in Tenterden Street, Bury, currently stand empty after being vacated by the school when it ‘rationalised and expanded’ its estate The premises are thought to date back to around 1927 when they served as a police station and courthouse. The site was bought by the Bury Grammar School in 1993, and was initially used as a junior boys’ school. Later, it became a sixth form centre Developer Property Investment Complete Ltd has now put forward proposals to convert what were the Main School Building, Arts Building and Sixth Form Building into new homes . Some 21 apartments are suggested for the site Of these, 14 could be created in the main building, two in the arts centre and five in the sixth form building. Add-ons are also proposed for the latter two buildings which would see the existing single-storey extensions increased to two storeys

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester City Centre Cafe bombarded with over 100 in-person applicants for part-time barista role Hospitality leaders have spoken out Add to preferred sources Comments News Paul Britton Reporter 14:14, 24 Oct 2026 View 3 Images The Fig & Sparrow (Im A city centre cafe was bombarded with more than 100 in-person applicants for a part-time barista role Hospitality leaders said the mass turn-out showed jobs are available in the sector - and potential employees are ready and willing to fill them - but that independent businesses should be given more Government support The Fig & Sparrow in Manchester's Northern Quarter said it was 'doing it differently this time' after the cafe received more than 400 emails from applicants during a previous recruitment appeal The 'walk-in' interviews were held on Tuesday, October 13. The inquest heard Jake's mental health concerns were 'overlooked' despite him being 'severely mentally unwell' when he was moved to Forest Bank from HMP Liverpool 18 days earlier At the time of his death Mr O'Brien, of Altrincham , Trafford , who was on remand for car crime offences, was in the process of being assessed for a transfer to a psychiatric hospital. Add to preferred sources Comments News Edward Barnes A community group fears plans to build homes next to a nature reserve could destroy a Stockport ‘gem’ forever. This week councillors considered plans for 181 new homes to be built off Jacksons Lane in Hazel Grove It is the latest plan put forward for consideration in the area after 160 homes were approved last month. The new plans promise to provide 91 homes that will be classed as affordable with 20 for social rent. The development would be entirely within the green belt and close to the The plans include funds for new open space as well as a £30,000 contribution to support nature within the reserve. There is also a promised £1.3m contribution towards education provision and £243,608 towards creating additional floorspace at possible three different medical centr However Deborah Hind, on behalf of the Friends of Happy Valley, said she was worried about the plan’s impact on the area and its wildlife which she was a ‘massive asset’ to the borough. If the plans are approved, she feared increased footfall would degrade the area over time She added: “We are about to devastate such an asset, such a gem in Stockport and I sound quite emotional because that’s what I am, because I just can’t believe that we’re allowing another development and people are going to walk down into that valley.”

He was then elected 13 years later in 1992 as the MP for However in 1997, that constituency was abolished due to boundary changes and Baron Davies was beaten in the Labour selection process for the new constituency of Oldham West and Royton by Michael Meacher. Later that year, he was given a life peerage in the House of Lords and subse He held this position until July 9 2024 where he was removed as a member because of non-attendance. The Association of Former Members of Parliament said he died in October 2026 Baron Davies served as Government Deputy Chief Whip in the House of Lords from 2003 to 2010, and as usual for a holder of that position, also held the position of Captain of the Yeomen of the Guard

The trio targeted people using ATMs in Halifax bank, including in the Stockport and Bury branches, and at Lloyds Bank Detectives found Matei, Ciubotaru and Mandache, who are all Romanian nationals, would travel across the country during their malicious enterprise. To trick their victims, one of the men would stand close enough to see them entering their pin into the cash machine Another would distract them by drawing attention to a banknote deliberately placed on the floor nearby, Cheshire Police said. The third man would then swipe their bank card and replace it with a similar-looking card Victims were left completely unaware that their card had been stolen. The gang would then use the stolen cards and PIN to withdraw cash and buy items, often before the victims had realised what had happened

The property on Old Hall Lane, Broughton Park, is described by experts as a "strikingly glamorous" house Built in 1935 it is a rare example of the international Streamline Moderne style that evolved from Art Deco. It features curved corners, long horizontal "speed lines," and a sleek, machine-age look inspired by ocean liners, airplanes, and trains Other examples of the style include East Finchley Tube Station in London and the Coca Cola building in Los Angeles. The design is characterised by flat roofs, horizontal emphasis, curved corners and dramatic glazing From the outside, this house is distinguished by slim brown brick facades, a flat roof, an exposed white concrete base, and windows that span both curved and angled corners View 5 Images A curved stair tower dominates the back of the house, while the entrance front steps back in stages, with an original single-storey garage reflecting the growing importance of the car in home design between the First and Second World Wars

Businesses in Rawtenstall are worried they may close for good if looming long-running roadworks bite too hard The Rossendale town's main Bank Street area will soon be hit by roadworks for the best part of a year. And the start comes at what should be a hectic time for independent businesses in the run-up to Christmas Pubs, bars, gift shops and tanning shops all fear the disruption will impact footfall at what should be their busiest season, Lancs Live reports . They have issued a plea for people to 'use them or lose them' in the months ahead Gary Horler runs Chuffin' Ale, a beer and wine shop on Bank Street which opened last year. He says he has been 'banding together' with other small businesses to raise concerns with local councillors and MPs about the roadworks and their expected impact But the outcome has not been welcomed. "We were previously assured that Christmas trade will not be jeopardised," Gary said

Simon Richardson denies murdering Michael Mullins Add to preferred sources A murder trial has heard of the tragic injuries Stretford Grammar headteacher Michael Mullins suffered after he was struck by a car and dragged for over a mile before dying at the side of he road Simon Richardson, 35, is alleged to have murdered Michael Mullins as he cycled home in April this year. Mr Richardson denies murder; an alternate offence of manslaughter; and dangerous driving and is on trial at Minshull Street Crown Court Prosecutors allege that Mr Richardson hit Mr Mullins in his Volvo in Altrincham on April 20. The 56-year-old headteacher was making his way home to Northwich after work when he was struck at the junction of Dunham Road and Warburton Lane, the court was told He was dragged under the wheels of the car for 1.3 miles - 2.2km - before dying at the roadside on Wet Gate Lane in Lymm. Mr Richardson, 35, earlier failed to properly observe a junction, 'flying straight through the give way markers', before hitting Mr Mullins, it is alleged Jurors heard that the defendant didn't stop and 'put his foot down'. Mr Mullins was trapped under the car while his damaged bike was left in the road

"Six months later we were happy as can be in Harpurhey and all the family fell in love with Manchester which had given us a home." Pat went on to devote his life to the city and its people. That bleak landscape of late-industrial Manchester Pat first saw in the 1950s would be utterly unrecognisable by the time the shattering news of his death was announced this week , aged 78 He played his own significant role in that transformation, becoming the face of the city centre and a fierce champion of its growth. Emergency services raced out to Holmes Chapel station at around 7.30pm on Tuesday evening (October 27) British Transport Police says it was called out to reports of a passenger suffering a medical emergency. The man, aged in his late 20s, was sadly pronounced dead at the scene The incident is not thought to be suspicious. A British Transport Police spokesperson said: "We were called to Holmes Chapel station at around 7.30pm on Tuesday, October 27 following reports of a passenger suffering a medical emergency on a train "Officers attended along with paramedics but despite their efforts sadly the person was pronounced dead at the scene. The incident is not being treated as suspicious and a file will be prepared for the coroner." Northern, Avanti West Coast and Transport for Wales running to and from Manchester Piccadilly were all subject to delays and cancellations on Tuesday night while emergency services worked at the scene. Clark Sinclair Limited took advantage of companies with debts by providing 'misleading services', the government's Insolvency Service has said The Manchester-registered company was found to be offering 'alternatives' to formal insolvency to directors of the companies in financial difficulty. It offered to arrange sales of 'financially distressed' businesses for £1 whilst charging fees of between £2,500 and £6,800 It comes following an Insolvency Service investigation which has subsequently led to the firm being shut down Insolvency Service Chief Investigator, David Usher, said: "Clark Sinclair Limited took advantage of struggling businesses by offering directors a misleading route out of their company’s debts, charging thousands of pounds for the service "Selling a company does not prevent its former directors’ conduct from being investigated if it later enters liquidation

But they’ve warned that there are more concerning From November 20, changes to Airbnb's ‘house rules’ policy will come into effect. From that date hosts will have to choose from seven standard rules, with anything else being stipulated as a request Under the updated policy, hosts can make ‘reasonable requests’ regarding cleaning and rubbish, however Airbnb has clarified on its website what hosts cannot ask. Under the new rules hosts can no longer ask guests to: wash dishes and put them away, strip the bed, remove rubbish of They can ask guests to put used dishes in the sink, gather together used towels and turn off amenities before leaving. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bury ‘Serious safety failings’ found in Bury council social housing inspection, watchdog warns The council could not show it was meeting the ‘legally required timescales’ to investigate, identify and repair hazards such as damp and mould, while 2,800 Outcomes in safety and accountability were judged to be particularly poor, with the Regulator of Social Housing saying it cannot be sure the town hall is meeting its legal duties. The town hall owns around 7,600 homes with some 300 of these managed by an external agency It was the council’s first inspection under the regulatory framework and it was awarded a C3 rating – the second lowest outcome. The council took its housing services back into direct management in 2024 as it began to wind down social housing provider Six Town Housing (STH) It is in the process of consulting on the future of the remaining around 100 homes managed by STH, with a recent report recommending that these too be brought under the council control. The council believes that will offer ‘greater long-term stability’ for tenants, with alternati Among the concerns raised by inspectors were overdue fire safety remedial actions, with 2,800 outstanding at the time of the inspection. The arrests come after officers were called to reports of a motor theft in the Wigan area around 10pm on Wednesday (October 28) Police spotted the stolen vehicle, leading to a police chase. The pursuit ended on Elliot Street where the van was involved in a collision at around 10.35pm The M.E.N understands the vehicle crashed into a Bee Network Bus on the main road. Download A major investment in specialist education has been completed at Millwood Primary School, creating additional places and state-of-the-art facilities for children with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND) in Bury The £13 million project has delivered a substantial new wing containing seven new classrooms, a multi-use hall, sensory rooms, a rebound room, non-teaching areas, external play spaces and additional car parking. The project has also included repairs to the school's roof and exist The scheme has been funded through capital allocations from the Department for Education which supports local authorities in their duty to provide suitable school placements for children and young people with SEND Creating more capacity at Millwood is a key part of Bury Council's plans to strengthen SEND provision across the borough. The expansion responds to increasing demand for specialist school places and will enable more children and young people to have their needs met closer to home The new facilities allow Millwood to cater for more than 200 primary-aged pupils with a range of additional educational needs and disabilities, providing high-quality learning environments designed to support pupils to thrive and achieve their full potential

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Residents in Saddleworth will have the opportunity to vote on the future of planning in their area when a referendum takes place on Thursday 10 December 2026. The referendum will ask residents whether they want Oldham Council and the Peak District National Park Authority to use the Saddleworth Neighbourhood Plan to help decide planning applications in the area. The plan sets out local planning policies for Saddleworth and, if approved, will become part of the area’s statutory Development Plan, helping to guide decisions on future planning applications. Residents will be asked the following question: “Do you want Oldham Council and the Peak District National Park Authority to use the Neighbourhood Plan for Saddleworth to help it decide planning applications in the neighbourhood area?” To vote, residents must be registered to vote in local government elections and have a qualifying address within the Saddleworth Neighbourhood Area. The deadline to register to vote is Tuesday 24 November 2026. Residents who wish to vote by post, proxy or who need a Voter Authority Certificate should also be aware of the following deadlines: - Wednesday 25 November, 5pm: Deadline for new postal vote applications and changes to existing postal voting arrangements. - Wednesday 2 December, 5pm: Deadline for new proxy vote applications and applications for a free Voter Authority Certificate. - Thursday 10 December, 5pm: Deadline for emergency proxy vote applications, where eligible. Residents can read the Saddleworth Neighbourhood Plan and supporting referendum documents online at: https://www.oldham.gov.uk/info/201235/neighbourhood_planning/2936/saddleworth_neighbourhood_plan Paper copies are also available to view at Lees, Uppermill, Delph and Greenfield libraries, Oldham Council’s reception

That depends who you ask… Tech by Chris Newbould November 4, 2026 Lecturers and students have significantly different perceptions of how much generative artificial intelligence (AI) is being used in university studies, according to new research from The University of Manchester and Spain’s Universidad del Pais Vasco/Euskal Herriko Unibertsitatea. The study found that academic staff perceived students to be using AI tools such as ChatGPT for their studies much more extensively than students reported themselves. Researchers say the findings highlight a gap in understanding between staff and students, at a time when universities are grappling with how best to respond to the technology. Academic staff rated their perception of students’ AI use at 5.23 out of seven, compared with an average of 3.11 among students reporting their own use for academic purposes. That's the biggest line-up yet, and they'll be selling art, jewellery, clothing, oddities, candles and all sorts of dark and lovely things you didn't kn It's also a strong shout for early Christmas shopping, especially for the person in your life who's impossible to buy for (we all have one...) It runs until 8pm so there's no rush on a Sunday afternoon. Parking is free on site, so no faffing about with town centre car parks either Catch up with Stockport Alternative Market on Facebook .
